title: Destatis Flash: Germany May 2026 Inflation Falls to 2.6% as Food Prices Drop, Energy Remains Elevated
detail: Germany's Federal Statistical Office (Destatis) released its preliminary consumer price inflation estimate for May 2026 on May 29, showing annual CPI at 2.6% — down from 2.9% in April 2026. The easing was driven by a sharp fall in food price inflation to 0.4% (from higher April levels) while goods inflation moderated to 2.2%. However, services inflation remained sticky at 3.1%, reflecting ongoing wage-growth pass-through in the labor-intensive sector. Energy prices rose 6.6% year-on-year, partly due to Middle East conflict-related supply disruptions — a trend flagged by the EU Commission's Spring 2026 Economic Forecast, which lowered Germany's full-year GDP growth forecast to 0.6% from the earlier estimate of 1.2%, specifically citing the energy price shock. The harmonised index of consumer prices (HICP) for May 2026 was projected at 2.7%. Destatis noted that final confirmed CPI data would be released on June 12, 2026. The inflation reading — while still above the ECB's 2% target — represented a welcome downward step after April's uptick and supported the ECB's cautious rate-cut trajectory. Germany's inflation has fallen dramatically from the 6.9% peak recorded during the 2022 post-Russian-gas-cutoff energy crisis.
